strategy.summary: Reproduce the column-order dependence of statsmodels.tools.tools.matrix_rank with method='qr' by running the developer's test_matrix_rank_column_order on the buggy commit 1e750ab0e99c (unpivoted scipy.linalg.qr) and on the fixed revision (scipy.linalg.qr with pivoting=True); the test should fail on buggy and pass on fixed, while ip and svd parametrizations act as controls that pass on both.

pinned_because: No documented scipy or numpy constraint is given in the evidence; versions are unbounded and left to the resolver, chosen by era-inferred reasoning only: use a scipy/numpy pair that is compatible with the statsmodels source at the buggy commit (the installation command given uses nightly wheels, which is an alternative but not required).

statsmodels itself is built from source at the buggy commit because the test imports the local tools module; INSTALL.txt requirements were not in the supplied passages, so the build requirements are inferred.

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/tools/tests/test_tools.py::test_matrix_rank_column_order, parametrized over method in ['ip','qr','svd']; for each of the six permutations of columns of exog = column_stack((ones(40), x, 2x)) with x = 1e3*arange(1,41)/7, asserts matrix_rank(exog[:, cols], method=method) == 2.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 1e750ab0e99c, the test_matrix_rank_column_order[qr] case fails (at least one permutation returns rank 3 instead of 2, triggering assert_equal with err_msg 'column order ...'), while [ip] and [svd] pass. On the fixed revision (pivoting=True in the qr call in tools.matrix_rank), all three parametrizations pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compute matrix_rank(exog[:, list(cols)], method='qr') for each of the six permutations of cols over range(3) and compare to 2; the transition is decided by whether any permutation returns 3 on the buggy revision.

input_output_examples.input: Three columns, one a multiple of another, in one of six column permutations of m
input_output_examples.buggy_output: rank 3 in one column order, rank 2 in the other five

risks: The bug is visible only when column scales differ widely (intercept of ones versus a 1e3-scale regressor); the test's construction is what exposes it, so do not substitute equal-scale columns.

The exact per-permutation rank values on the buggy revision are not stated beyond the commit message claim (rank 3 in one order, rank 2 in five); the failing permutation is therefore not known in advance.

Floating-point behaviour of LAPACK QR (BLAS/LAPACK backend of the installed scipy, e.g. OpenBLAS vs MKL) can change the diagonal magnitudes and thus whether the unpivoted tolerance crosses the threshold; a different numerical backend may not reproduce the failure, and this platform dependence is not characterised in the evidence.
The buggy commit's numpy/scipy versions are not documented; a newer scipy may change qr defaults or rounding and mask the defect, so version selection is an inference that could fail to reproduce.

Only the test diff and the commit message are evidence; the fixed revision's exact diff beyond tools.py lines 516-526 is not supplied, so the fixed-revision checkout must be taken from the PR merge state.

The control methods ip and svd are not expected to change; if they fail on the buggy revision the environment (not the qr path) is the likely cause and should be investigated before attributing the failure to the fix.
Failing on buggy is required for the transition; the test also requires the whole parametrized case to pass on fixed, so unrelated failures in the same file would obscure the result.

oracle.reference_source: test asserts integer rank equality to 2 via assert_equal
oracle.why: Rank is an integer count, so the oracle is exact equality rather than a numerical tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, matrix_rank with method='qr' uses unpivoted QR, so for some column order the R diagonal is not sorted and the tolerance keyed to the first diagonal element counts an extra diagonal entry, returning 3 instead of 2; assert_equal fails with err_msg 'column order (...)'.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With pivoting=True, the diagonal of R is ordered by decreasing magnitude and tol is keyed to the largest diagonal element, so the rank is 2 for all six permutations for ip, qr and svd, and the test passes.
